stem:
Sana hangs one iron chain outdoors in open rain. She keeps a second iron chain in a sealed dry box indoors. She coats a third iron chain with paint. She also leaves a copper wire outdoors in the same rain.

Answer both parts.

options.text: The outdoor iron chain can rust because air and water both reach it; the sealed dry chain does not; paint can help prevent rust on iron; the copper wire does not form the same brown iron rust.
The sealed dry iron chain rusts because dry air alone is enough.
The copper wire develops the same brown iron rust outdoors in rain.
The brown paint coating on the third chain is itself rust.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Iron rusts only when both air and water are present; keeping iron dry or coating it with paint can prevent rust, and copper does not form brown iron rust.

teacher.key_rationale: Rusting of iron needs both air and water. Dry sealed storage and paint prevent contact that leads to rust. Copper is not iron, so it does not form the same brown rust; paint is a coating, not rust.
